model_annotations.Bulgarian: Тази стълбовидна диаграма (Figure 5) илюстрира сравнение на перплексията при два метода — per-output и per-layer — при различни нива на разреденост (sparsity rates). Хоризонталната ос представя категориите на нивата на разреденост, които вероятно съответстват на стойностите 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70% и 80%, подредени в нарастващ ред отляво надясно, макар че конкретните етикети по тази ос не са ясно видими на изображението. Вертикалната ос представя стойностите на перплексията, като съгласно описанието под фигурата е използвана логаритмична скала поради значителната разлика в стойностите между ниските и високите нива на разреденост. За всяко ниво на разреденост са представени по два стълба — един в оранжев цвят, съответстващ на единия метод, и един в по-тъмен (кафяв или тъмнооранжев) цвят, съответстващ на другия метод, като групирането е по двойки за всяка категория на разреденост. При ниските нива на разреденост (в лявата част на диаграмата) стълбовете са с относително ниска и сходна височина, докато при по-високите нива на разреденост (в дясната част) височината на стълбовете нараства значително, като последната двойка стълбове при 80% разреденост е видимо най-висока, като единият от стълбовете в тази двойка е забележимо по-висок от другия. Съгласно придружаващата таблица (Table 13), стойностите на перплексията за per-output метода варират от 5.70 при 10% до 534.12 при 80%, а за per-layer метода — от 5.70 при 10% до 886.10 при 80%. Диаграмата не съдържа видима легенда директно върху изображението, но контекстът от описанието под фигурата указва, че двата цвята съответстват на per-output и per-layer методите.
model_annotations.Chinese: This figure presents a comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates, as indicated by the caption (Figure 5), with the note that logarithmic results are used for comparison due to the significant difference in values between high and low sparsity rates. The horizontal axis represents different sparsity rates, though the specific percentage labels along this axis are not clearly legible in the image; based on the accompanying table, these likely correspond to 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%. The vertical axis appears to represent perplexity values on a logarithmic scale, though the axis labels and tick marks are not clearly visible. The chart contains two sets of bars at each sparsity level, forming grouped pairs. One set of bars appears in a tan or light beige color, representing one method (likely Per-Output), while the other set appears in a darker orange or brown color, representing the other method (likely Per-Layer). At the lower sparsity rates on the left side of the chart, the bars are very short and nearly identical in height between the two methods, reflecting the close perplexity values (e.g., 5.70 and 5.70 at 10%). As sparsity increases moving rightward, the bars grow progressively taller, with the rightmost bars at 80% sparsity being dramatically taller than all others, consistent with the sharp increase in perplexity values reported in the table (534.12 for Per-Output and 886.10 for Per-Layer). The bars appear to be arranged in ascending order from left to right corresponding to increasing sparsity rates, and the overall visual pattern shows an exponential-like growth in bar height toward the higher sparsity levels, with the final group of bars being substantially taller than all preceding groups.
model_annotations.English: This bar chart, labeled as Figure 5, illustrates the comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates, with logarithmic values used for comparison due to the significant difference in values between high and low sparsity rates. The horizontal axis represents different sparsity rates, which appear to correspond to the percentages 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%, arranged from left to right in ascending order. The vertical axis represents the logarithmic perplexity values, though specific axis labels and tick marks are not clearly visible in the chart. The bars are presented in grouped pairs at each sparsity level, with one bar in a light tan or beige color representing the per-output method and the other in a darker orange or brown color representing the per-layer method. At lower sparsity rates (10% through approximately 40%), the paired bars are relatively short and similar in height, reflecting the close perplexity values reported in the accompanying table (e.g., 5.70 and 5.70 at 10%, 5.81 and 5.82 at 20%). As sparsity increases beyond 50%, the bars grow progressively taller, with the per-layer bars becoming noticeably taller than the per-output bars, particularly at 70% and 80% sparsity, where the per-output values are 20.46 and 534.12 and the per-layer values are 39.02 and 886.10, respectively. The tallest bars appear at the 80% sparsity level on the far right, where both bars are dramatically taller than all others, reflecting the exponential increase in perplexity at high sparsity. The bars are not sorted independently but follow the natural ascending order of sparsity rates, and no bars appear to be specially emphasized through outlining or annotation beyond the color distinction between the two methods.
model_annotations.German: Das Diagramm (Figure 5) zeigt einen Vergleich der Per-Output- und Per-Layer-Perplexität bei verschiedenen Sparsity-Raten, wobei aufgrund der erheblichen Wertunterschiede zwischen hohen und niedrigen Sparsity-Raten eine logarithmische Skala für den Vergleich verwendet wird. Die horizontale Achse stellt die verschiedenen Sparsity-Raten dar, die von links nach rechts in aufsteigender Reihenfolge angeordnet sind (10 %, 20 %, 30 %, 40 %, 50 %, 60 %, 70 %, 80 %), während die vertikale Achse die Perplexitätswerte auf einer logarithmischen Skala darstellt, wobei keine expliziten Achsenbeschriftungen oder Tick-Markierungen im Diagramm sichtbar sind. Für jede Sparsity-Rate sind zwei Balken gruppiert nebeneinander dargestellt: Der linke Balken in einem hellen Beige- oder Sandton repräsentiert die Per-Output-Methode, und der rechte Balken in einem dunkleren Orange- oder Braunton repräsentiert die Per-Layer-Methode. Bei den niedrigen Sparsity-Raten (10 % und 20 %) sind die Balken beider Methoden nahezu gleich hoch und sehr niedrig, entsprechend den Perplexitätswerten von etwa 5,70 bzw. 5,81–5,82. Mit zunehmender Sparsity-Rate wachsen die Balken progressiv in der Höhe, wobei bei den mittleren Raten (30 %–50 %) die Per-Output-Balken geringfügig kürzer erscheinen als die Per-Layer-Balken, was den Werten aus der zugehörigen Tabelle entspricht (z. B. 5,99 vs. 6,03 bei 30 %, 6,38 vs. 6,56 bei 40 %, 7,17 vs. 7,70 bei 50 %). Bei den höheren Sparsity-Raten (60 %, 70 %, 80 %) steigen die Balkenhöhen deutlich an, wobei die Per-Output-Balken bei 60 % einen Wert von etwa 9,35 gegenüber 10,95 für Per-Layer aufweisen, bei 70 % etwa 20,46 gegenüber 39,02 und bei 80 % etwa 534,12 gegenüber 886,10, sodass die höchsten Balken bei 80 % Sparsity die mit Abstand größten im Diagramm sind. Die Balken sind in aufsteigender Reihenfolge der Sparsity-Rate von links nach rechts angeordnet, und es sind keine besonderen visuellen Hervorhebungen wie Umrandungen oder Anmerkungen an einzelnen Balken erkennbar.
